issues.note: Country sense has its own definition and collocations; splitting it is defensible. Taste only.
In 'at home', home is the object of 'at', so a noun. No contradiction.
The British region label on the phrase is correct; 'variant phrase' has no basis.
'Is Sam home?' (adverb) and 'at home' (noun) are consistent analyses.
The correction should be 'She went back home.'
General American is hoʊm; hum is wrong.
Confused claim that mixes in a verb use; sense 3 already covers 'into place'.
'used to describe the act of' is banned padding in a content-word definition.

findings.F1: American IPA given as hum instead of hoʊm.
findings.F2: Learner-error correction 'went back to the home' is wrong; should be 'went back home'.
findings.F3: Sense 1 definition padded with 'used to describe the act of' instead of a direct adverb phrase.

missed: The 'no preposition before home after verbs of movement' fact is stated four times (sense 1 explanation, usage note, learner-error note, grammar adaptation note), against one fact, one field.
